Results table with NES, p-value, FDR q-value per hallmark pathway exported
Significant pathways (FDR q < 0.25 per standard GSEA convention, or q<0.05 if stricter reporting desired) listed with direction (up in lesional vs control)
Enrichment plots for top pathways saved

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples) comparing 6 atopic dermatitis lesional skin samples vs 6 control skin samples, unpaired, single batch. sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, so it must be flagged and handled with sensitivity analysis rather than silently dropped or silently kept. The plan: (1) QC the count matrix and metadata, quantify the sample_01 depth issue and decide/document a handling strategy (down-weighting via DESeq2's built-in size-factor normalization plus an explicit sensitivity run excluding sample_01); (2) run DESeq2-equivalent differential expression in Python (pydeseq2) on the full 6v6 design, and a leave-one-out sensitivity comparison excluding sample_01, to check whether DE results are driven by that sample; (3) run pre-ranked GSEA against the MSigDB human hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC symbols) using the DE result's ranking statistic; (4) synthesize DE genes and hallmark pathways into a decision-ready summary, explicitly reporting genes/pathways whose significance depends on sample_01. All steps use Python only per user constraint (pydeseq2 for DE, gseapy/blitzgsea-compatible prerank GSEA). Reference data used: MSigDB human hallmark gene sets (h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, 50 sets, HGNC symbols) confirmed present and organism-matched (human).
